subject: geography
title: Ice Ages and Glaciers
welcome_lead: Imagine Britain buried under a mile of ice! Discover ice ages and the rivers of ice called glaciers.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on ice ages and how glaciers form.
final_note: Brilliant! You now understand how glaciers work.

walkthroughs.body_html: During the last ice age (ending ~10,000 years ago), much of Britain was buried under glaciers. We are now in a warmer interglacial period.
Snow piles up in cold mountain areas, compresses into ice, and flows slowly downhill — a glacier. They move just metres per year but reshape mountains!
Plucking: ice freezes to rocks and rips them loose. Abrasion: trapped rocks scratch and grind the bedrock — like giant sandpaper.

mcqs.q: What are the four pillars of food security?
options: Food security just means producing enough food.
Availability (enough food exists), access (people can obtain it), utilisation (nutritional quality and absorption) and stability (consistent over time) — defined by the FAO.

mcqs.q: How do scientists know current climate change is anthropogenic?
options: Food security means storing food for emergencies.
Isotopic signatures of CO2 match fossil fuel sources, warming patterns (cooler stratosphere, warmer troposphere) match greenhouse forcing, and natural forcings cannot explain the rate.
Climate change is caused by the sun getting hotter.
Climate change is mainly caused by natural Milankovitch cycles.
